practice_sentences.en: Why do you (m) think that he will buy this cheap shirt? He told me that he only likes expensive clothes.

answer_key.translit: lesh btfaker eno rah yeshtri hal-qamees el-rkhees? howa qalli eno bas bihebb el-malabes el-ghalyea

practice_sentences.en: Yesterday, she took my book and put it behind the chair in the living room, but I didn't see it until now.

review_flags.note: Almost certainly 'Cat' (bisse). Fix the English gloss.
Means near/close (distance). 'To close' is a different verb (asaker, L17).
'ila' leans MSA; everyday Levantine often uses '3a' / 'la' (barooh 3al mat3am).
Notes mostly give bare forms (ana aroh). Everyday Levantine statements usually add b- (ana barooh, howa byakol); bare form after bedi / lazem / rah. The app should accept and teach both contexts.
Likely 'mudiri byiji mit2akhkhir kil yom' (my boss comes late every day).
